en: So Aoyama got Watase to come to Fukuoka as leverage for the negotiations.
There's one thing I still don't know.
Whether Daigo knew about Aoyama's plans.
Huh? That's hard to say for sure.
Did Chairman Dojima hint at anything?
When Daigo was in my cab, I could tell he was willing to put his life on the line for this to succeed.
Given his resolve, would he really have been okay bringing a wild card like the Watase Family to a clan negotiation?
If my hunch is right, there's only one man who could be responsible for his disappearance.
You don't mean Patriarch Aoyama!?
Patriarch Aoyama left to negotiate with Patriarch Madarame. As acting chairman.
What? Where!?
North of Nagasugai. Yamagasa Family headquarters!
Y'need somethin', old man? This here's private property.
My name is Suzuki from Nagasu Taxi.
Yeah? And what's a taxi driver doin' here?
We got a call for a pickup. Nobody told you?
Naw, I didn't hear a thing about no taxi.
Strange. The call was from an Aoyama-san of the Tojo Clan.
The Tojo Clan, huh?
That's right, sir. It sounded urgent.
I don't think he'd be happy to hear I was late because of you.
Oh, er... yeah.
All right, lemme check on that real quick. Stay put, y'hear?
Let's move.
Patriarch Aoyama! What have you done?
I thought you'd come. You sure took your sweet time.
So, you're Aoyama.
What's going on here? We're supposed to be swearing an oath with the Yamagasa, not murdering their patriarch.
Hmph. It doesn't take a genius to figure out I'd never settle for such humiliation. Isn't that why you're here? To stop me?
The truth is, I never had the slightest intention of an alliance with the Yamagasa.
My plan was to dangle a tempting amount of cash in their faces, then slowly wring their necks.
I can see how our friend here lasted so long as chairman, even if he was merely the head of a backwoods family.
It seems Madarame was on to me from the very beginning.
All it took was a moment's distraction and he already had his gun trained on me.
Fortunately for me, he missed. So I took him down with the knife I always keep on my person.
But why? Why are you doing this?
You know why. The mighty rock that is the Tojo Clan has no business with pebbles like the Yamagasa.
But Chairman Dojima wanted this alliance to go through. Are you really going to go behind his back on this?
Chairman Dojima? I believe you mean <Italic>former</Italic> chairman.
I said I'm in charge of the Tojo Clan now. And so long as the chairman remains missing, whatever I say goes.
It's pretty simple, as I see it. In the yakuza ocean, you either eat or be eaten.
Why waste time negotiating when we could be swallowing the Yamagasa whole? It's only logical.
And whether it's Dojima or Kiryu, the same rule applies. Once you've given up the throne, you're nothing more than a relic of the past.
I appreciate you showing up last night. Though I hear you ended up butting heads with my captain, Yahata.
Glad to see you're okay.
In no small part thanks to the bulletproof vest I was wearing. It surely saved my life.
In truth, I was warned this might happen. That these Tojo Clan dealings were not all they seemed to be.
Someone warned you?
That's right. A very particular person.
He said if he were to go missing, and if someone else from the Tojo Clan approached me afterward, that "someone" would betray me.
Go missing? You can't mean⑬
Yes. I was forewarned by none other than Daigo Dojima-san.
Is this suitable, Chairman Dojima?
Yes. You have my thanks for arranging the car, Patriarch Madarame.
I was surprised you contacted us directly to cancel the hotel meeting, not to mention suggesting a private car as the new location.
Was there some kind of problem?
This is difficult for me to say for sure...
But it's highly likely that one, or both, of our lives was in danger.
Hm. That is indeed disconcerting.
Every detail of today's meeting at the Nagasu Grand Hotel was organized by the Tojo Clan.
And yet, something felt wrong.
Wrong? In what way?
Usually, negotiations like this are done on the outskirts of town where they are less visible, in a room with only small windows.
It always pays to safeguard against attacks or assassination attempts from nearby buildings.
But that hotel is in the middle of Nagasugai.
What's more, the meeting was set to take place in a suite with large windows.
You're almost asking to get shot if you hold talks at a location like that.
Not to mention, that hotel is practically a labyrinth. It would be impossible to seal off.
If the police or another group raided the place, there's no chance we could cover all the entry points.
Taking yakuza customs into account, the venue chosen defied any semblance of common sense in the matter.
In other words, it would have been a killing field.
Are you telling me that one of your men planned to betray the organization? Is that right?
Yes. This alliance has met no small amount of opposition from the rank and file clan members.
To that end, Patriarch Madarame. I have a favor to ask.
After we leave this car, I want you to stick to the story I'm about to tell you. That, and...
Please forgive me for disappearing after this.
Disappearing?
(The people of this town have been good to me. I've got to stop this war for their sake, too.)
(I should take care of any unfinished business, then go and see the chief.)
(Nakajima-san gave me another lease on life. I can't let anything happen to him.)
(Time to settle things here.)
Come one, come all! Witness the most revolutionary technological marvel of our time! Step right up and try your hand at IF8!
(Hm? What's that all about?)
Try the latest and greatest sensation in all of arcade gaming! We'll be at the parking lot in southwest Nagasugai for a limited time only!
(Sounds like some kind of event. Maybe I'll go check it out later.)
(It's only right Nakajima-san knows the truth, with the impact this'll have on him. I should go to the office and settle things.)
(So Madarame wants to break up the Yamagasa Family. Better tell Yahata about this.)
(And if I'm going to find him, I should start by tracking down his men. They were all wearing those tacky red tracksuits, if I remember right.)
There. That was the last of them!
Seems so. Man, they didn't even hesitate to attack ya, huh?
And you're from the same family as they are...
Yeah, crazy... I didn't recognize any of them, though.
They must have joined the family after I was gone. That was ten years ago.
Yeah? Ya miss it?
Things... are different now, compared to when I left.
There really is no place I can call home anymore.
It's a sad thing.
We should go. Come on, this way.
What're we gonna do here?
We can travel through the sewers if we go down this manhole.
And we wanna do that why?
At the ceremony site, there's a manhole right where the stage is located.
If we start here, we can approach the stage without being detected.
This is the best chance we've got at getting close to Kitakata.
How'd you figure that out?
I used to play at that park when I was a kid. I remember every last detail of the place.
How 'bout that? Let's do it!
Sir, can I check your bag?
(We ain't gettin' through the main streets, that's for sure.)
(Got no choice. The alleys, it is.)
Eh!?
Just as expected.
Haha, we knew that checkpoint would spook you and send you this way.
You Kitakata?
You got it. Man, I can't believe you actually busted out of Abashiri... Respect, dude.
All this talk of the legendary hitman might actually have some truth to it.
But you're not getting past me. Sorry, but no vengeance for your wormy little pal Majima!
The Kitakata Family will never kneel to the Tojo Clan!
Hey, you got the time?
The time.
It's... it's a bit after 11:30.
Then I ain't got time to dawdle.
I'll hafta finish this quick, then.
Hah! You think you're clever?
When I'm through with you, you won't be clever enough to scratch your ass!
Let's get him!
(Security's awful tight. Better check out the place today.)
(This has gotta be where they'll do the snow festival's opening ceremony.)
(So, how do we nab Kitakata tomorrow?)
(A manhole. Where does it lead to?)
(That's all the scoutin' I can do. Better meet up with Baba at Polaris and plan for tomorrow.)
(Alright, got some intel on Kitakata. Now back to Polaris!)
(This phone booth... It's the one in the photo.)
(Guess I'm s'posed to answer it.)
Go to the lottery kiosk. The passcode is "seven scattered losing tickets."
*click* *dial tone*
(I need a pass for the casino, eh? Bet that old homeless guy Kiyotaka has one.)
Saejima-san! What a relief. Did you have trouble getting here?
Nah. So, this the hideout you were talkin' about?
Yes. It's just up here.
Hold up. There's a cop.
Damn. Can't go this way.
Baba, you saw the news. My face is plastered everywhere.
If we stay together, you'll get burned, too. Let's split up and meet at yer hideout.
But then you...
Don't worry 'bout me. I'm used to this sorta thing. How's yer pain? Still as bad as it was on the mountain?
Uh, I...
This cold's real bad if you're in pain. Hurry on to the hideout. Ya got your own health to worry about before ya go motherin' me.
...Okay, I'll do that. I'm sorry, Aniki.
So, where's this hideout?
There's a major street that runs north to south through the town center. It's called Central Station Boulevard, and there's a Don Quijote on it.
The hideout is a bar called <Color:7>Polaris<Color:Default>, in the building across the street.
Gotcha. I'll see ya later.
Please be careful, Aniki.
(All right, across the street from Don Quijote on Central Station Boulevard. Can't be that hard to find.)
I took a look around. It's not good.
There are a lot of cops. It's too risky to use the main road to go straight to the hideout.
So what now?
I'll go on ahead.
You follow me, but at a distance. We'll try not to draw attention.
Final preparations for Tsukimino's Snow Festival are underway at Main Street Park, where many are working hurriedly to finish before tomorrow night's opening.
Each year, the famous winter event attracts a sizable number of visitors from across Japan.
Local businesses are looking forward to this much-needed influx of tourist money.
And now, an update on the penitentiary fire.
The Prefectural Police made an announcement regarding the two missing convicts.
The remains of one convict were found this morning in the mountains surrounding the prison.
An arrest warrant has been issued for the other inmate, thought to still be in the area.
That inmate's name is Taiga Saejima, a former member of the Tojo Clan, and wanted nationwide.
Acting on tips that Saejima may appear in Sapporo, the police have gone on full alert in the Tsukimino area.
(Dammit...)
There was a fire at Abashiri?
And that body they found... who was that?
Uh, by the way, the hideout's ready.
That do the trick, Kiryu-san?
Yeah. Perfect.
Why tomorrow night, though? Those dirtbags ain't stupid.
We give 'em a chance to regroup, we ain't got a hope in hell of comin' outta there alive.
I'm aware. But I need some time to sort a few things out.
Those complications y'were talkin' about before I called up Aoyama?
Yeah. A lot of people here helped me out not knowing who I was. I have to set things straight so I don't make things worse for them.
Bet they'd practically shit 'emselves if they found out yer the Dragon of Dojima 'imself.
Gotta wonder why the boss never told us.
Patriarch Madarame was just protecting me. And Daigo, too.
Yeah, he helps out a little too much I reckon.
Maybe he really ain't cut out for yakuza life.
Heh. We're always the ones getting shafted for it anyhow.
Well, people like me and Madarame always seem to end up dragged into some mess or another.
I guess that's just our lot in life.
Guess so. Anyway, I'll go round up what's left of our boys and prep fer tomorrow night.
How 'bout you, Kiryu-san?
I'll meet you at the pier when it's time. If that works for you.
C-Captain!
Get back!
This is between me and him. You stay outta this.
Don't take it too hard. You can't be fighting at your best after that explosion earlier.
I know that, asshole.
But if I don't do nothin', the Tojo Clan's gonna rip Fukuoka out from under us.
I gotta get back at Aoyama for this, no matter what it takes.
Like I said, I won't let the Yamagasa Family fall apart.
But how're y'gonna do that?
